headline: Manchester United finally land Mauricio Pochettino after a decade of near misses
facts: Pochettino signed a two-year deal as United head coach.
United had circled him several times before: a 2016 lunch with Ferguson, the 2018 job after Mourinho, the 2021-22 search and a 2024 interview.
He replaces Michael Carrick, who got a two-year permanent deal in May and was sacked after 15 games.
background: Pochettino was Tottenham manager when United first looked at him in 2018 and was coaching the US national team when he finally got the job.
footage_terms: Pochettino Manchester United first press conference

headline: United CEO Berrada explains why Carrick was sacked after the Bournemouth defeat
facts: Carrick was sacked in the November international break, after a 3-0 home loss to Bournemouth on 25 October raised pressure.
Berrada said the club wanted to judge the team until the break and called the decision very difficult.
He said United spent 163m pounds this summer, mostly on midfielders Baleba, Tielemans and Santos, and defended the lack of defensive signings.
background: Carrick finished third last season and qualified United for the Champions League, which earned him a permanent contract.

headline: Drone video of Pochettino's first United training session spreads online
facts: A drone filmed 12 minutes of Pochettino's first Carrington session, including tactical drills, before the Liverpool game.
The operator apologised, called it a total error of judgement and took the video down, but reposts on X passed eight million views.
United have put up No Drones signs and will not sue this time; Iraola said such footage should not be legal.
background: Liverpool last beat United at Anfield 7-0 in March 2023; Pochettino's first game in charge is there on 22 November.
footage_terms: Pochettino first training session Man United

headline: Pochettino tells United players to relearn how to win as club sits 18th
facts: United are 18th with one league win and eight league games without a win.
It is their worst start to a season in 40 years, one point behind 17th-placed Coventry.
Pochettino, 54, said belief must come back through hard work and told players to treat pressure as energy.
background: Pochettino has been named in United talks for ten years; his previous job was national team coach of the United States.
footage_terms: Pochettino Man United players must relearn winning

headline: Iraola's Liverpool: chaos, man-marking and a fixed set-piece defence
facts: Liverpool are fourth after 10 league games with two defeats, but have won only once at Anfield.
Their pressing figure (PPDA) is 9.7, against 11.5 under Slot, and they average 50.8 long passes per game.
They have conceded two set-piece goals so far, after 23 under Slot last season.
background: Iraola took over in June 2026 after three seasons at Bournemouth; Slot lost his job after Liverpool finished fifth as defending champions.

headline: Thomas Frank returns at Crystal Palace and jokes about his Arsenal coffee cup
facts: Frank's first Palace game is away at Coventry; Palace are bottom, two points behind Coventry.
Palace have conceded the most goals in the league and striker Mateta is suspended.
He joked about avoiding another cup controversy and hinted there is more to tell about his Spurs spell.
background: In January, as Tottenham manager, Frank was seen drinking from an Arsenal-logo cup before a Bournemouth match, and Spurs sacked him in February after less than eight months.
footage_terms: Thomas Frank Crystal Palace press conference

headline: Crystal Palace sack Pierre Sage while bottom of the Premier League
facts: Sage won two of 10 Premier League games and Palace had conceded 24 goals, the most in the division.
He lasted about five months of a three-year deal after being hired in June 2026.
Squad cost limits forced summer sales and centre-back replacements arrived after the season began.
background: Sage won the Coupe de France with Lens and took them to a second-place Ligue 1 finish; Glasner had left Palace after criticising the board over the Guehi sale to Manchester City.

headline: Hurzeler commits to Brighton despite Manchester United rumours
facts: Hurzeler said he is fully committed to Brighton and called the links rumours.
Chairman Tony Bloom said he would fight ridiculously hard to keep him.
Brighton are second in the Premier League; United had considered Hurzeler as a Carrick replacement.
background: Hurzeler is in a strong season at Brighton and gets good reviews; United instead appointed Pochettino.

headline: De Zerbi answers Tottenham fans after Mudryk's Arsenal podcast comments
facts: On a podcast, Chelsea loanee Mudryk said Arsenal was his dream club and that he nearly joined them in 2023.
De Zerbi said he understands fan frustration but called Mudryk a good person and player; he would not discuss ending the loan in January.
Mudryk has played 16 minutes for Spurs and has an ankle injury; De Zerbi serves a touchline ban against Ipswich.
background: Mudryk picked Chelsea over Arsenal in the 2023 transfer window and has spoken publicly about a past drugs ban.
footage_terms: Mudryk Guest of Gordon podcast Arsenal

headline: Pochettino leaves USMNT after 8-0 aggregate win over Haiti; Arena says federation has no clue
facts: Pochettino's last USMNT game was a 2-0 win over Haiti on 17 November, 8-0 on aggregate in the Nations League quarterfinal.
He left less than three months after signing a new US Soccer contract.
Under-23 coach Steve Cherundolo will lead a December camp and a friendly against Jamaica while the search goes on.
background: Arena, who coached the US to a 2002 World Cup quarterfinal and missed the 2018 World Cup, had opposed hiring a foreign coach.

headline: Arteta says Arsenal will stop players leaking team news through Fantasy Premier League
facts: Arteta said confidentiality underpins trust and players will not be allowed to pick themselves.
A player picked and captained himself before the Liverpool game, then transferred himself out the next week.
Saliba is back from a back injury; Saka is out about another month with a quad problem.
background: Chelsea had earlier warned staff about Fantasy use after people linked to the club sold Joao Pedro in October, before his thigh injury became public.
footage_terms: Arsenal Fantasy Premier League team news leak

headline: Guimaraes grows at Arsenal but Arteta wants more before Newcastle return
facts: Guimaraes, a 75m pound signing from Newcastle, is now first choice after a slow start and an early injury.
Arteta said he is still not there but hitting serious levels and wants more impact in the box.
Arsenal visit Newcastle on 21 November, Guimaraes's return to St James' Park.
background: Guimaraes scored nine Premier League goals last season; Rice has said it can take a year to adapt to Arteta's demands.

headline: Ten lessons from Xabi Alonso's first ten Premier League games at Chelsea
facts: Chelsea have four league defeats and are 11 points behind Arsenal, but are seen as well placed for Champions League qualification.
Alonso has used back threes and back fours and six different central midfield combinations, and sometimes played without a striker.
Chelsea have scored 19 goals from an expected 15.9; Joao Pedro has five goals in six league starts and is injured.
background: Alonso's Chelsea have been described as consistently inconsistent, with only two back-to-back league wins in ten games.

headline: Enzo Maresca has a midfield balance problem at Manchester City
facts: City won their first seven games in all competitions, then lost their last three Premier League games.
The analysis says the team is too open and Fernandez's positioning leaves Elliot Anderson exposed in the double pivot.
City spent over 320m pounds rebuilding the midfield this summer; options discussed include Bouaddi as a screening six.
background: Maresca's City were unbeaten in their first seven games before the three-game league slide.

headline: Mourinho tells Vinicius to move on from his summer excuses
facts: Vinicius said he trained less than usual after the World Cup; Mourinho said he dislikes criticising honesty but wants him to move on.
Vinicius has one goal in eight LaLiga games and lost his place to record signing Yan Diomande.
He served a four-match ban after a red card against Villarreal and signed a contract to 2032 this summer.
background: Mourinho left Benfica after last season, where Porto won the Portuguese title, and his agent confirmed Real Madrid contact before he returned.

headline: Amorim blames himself after Milan lose 2-0 at home to Ferencvaros
facts: Milan lost 2-0 at San Siro in the Europa League despite Ferencvaros going down to ten men on 77 minutes.
Milan have three points from four league-phase games and sit 28th.
Amorim said there were no excuses and that he may have done something wrong.
background: Amorim is a former Manchester United manager who lost his job there in January.

headline: Bournemouth beat Amorim's Milan 3-0 in their first home European game
facts: Milan keeper Maignan was sent off on 27 minutes for shoving Tyler Adams.
Kluivert and Tavernier scored penalties and Adli added a free kick.
Bournemouth had won one of their first seven league games under Rose before beating Sunderland the weekend before.
background: Rose replaced Iraola in the summer; Bournemouth waited 127 years for European football.

headline: Allegri accepts two-match ban for insulting referee after Napoli draw with Roma
facts: Allegri, 59, got a two-match ban and a 10,000 euro fine after a red card in the 3-3 home draw with Roma.
He will miss the trip to Juventus, his former club.
Napoli have won three of eight Serie A games and are 11 points behind leaders Inter.
background: Allegri is a former Juventus coach, and Napoli are 11 points behind leaders Inter.

headline: Bayern coach Kompany out since collapsing at a training session
facts: Kompany collapsed at a reserve training session on 23 October and was treated for meningeal irritation.
Assistant Aaron Danks has run the team for five games and says Kompany is well on the way to full recovery.
Bayern have a policy of not involving him in football decisions while he recovers.
background: Harry Kane reportedly became the first Bayern player in 45 years to win the Ballon d'Or and signed a new deal.

headline: Luis Enrique becomes PSG's winningest coach with 127th win
facts: PSG beat Le Havre 5-1 and Luis Enrique passed Laurent Blanc with his 127th win.
Hakimi scored his first hat-trick and added two assists.
It was PSG's ninth straight win in all competitions; Dembele and Kvaratskhelia are injured.
background: PSG are the reigning French and European champions.

headline: Dirk Kuyt leaves Fenerbahce a week after beating Liverpool
facts: Kuyt left after Fenerbahce agreed a deal with Emre Belozoglu, a former club captain.
His last game as interim coach was a 3-2 Champions League win over Liverpool in Istanbul.
Fenerbahce are sixth in the Turkish league and 19th in the Champions League table.
background: Kuyt played for Fenerbahce from 2012 to 2015 and rejoined in July as assistant to Ismail Kartal, who resigned in October.

headline: Fabregas warns Como about hype after 9-1 Champions League win over Lens
facts: Como won 9-1, a record for goals scored away in the Champions League.
Tasos Douvikas scored a hat-trick and Nico Paz added a goal and two assists.
Fabregas said the team must not buy into its own hype; Como are fourth in Serie A.
background: Como is a Serie A club from an Italian luxury resort town, and this is its first season in European competition; Fabregas played for Arsenal, Barcelona and Chelsea.

headline: Ronaldo retires from Portugal duty after a row with coach Jorge Jesus
facts: Ronaldo, 41, announced his last game for Portugal; he holds the men's record of 146 international goals.
In September he left camp after being an unused substitute against Norway and said Jesus broke two promises.
Jesus said the coach decides and rules are the same for everyone; Portugal won their next two games without him.
background: Ronaldo has a long record of rows with coaches, including Mourinho at Real Madrid and Rangnick at Manchester United.

headline: Simeone backs Julian Alvarez after big misses in Atletico's loss to Barcelona
facts: Atletico lost 2-1 at home; Fermin Lopez scored both Barcelona goals.
Alvarez missed several chances, including a one-on-one with Joan Garcia.
Atletico's seven-game league winning streak ended and they sit third, five points behind Barcelona.
background: Alvarez wanted to leave for Barcelona in June, was jeered by Atletico fans at the start of the season and has since apologised.

headline: West Ham sack Nuno and hire Scott Parker, who draws 3-3 at Cardiff on day one
facts: Parker signed a two-and-a-half-year deal and managed Cardiff away the same day.
West Ham trailed 3-0 by the 39th minute to a Jack Moylan hat-trick and drew 3-3.
Nuno was sacked after a 3-1 loss to West Brom with West Ham eighth in the Championship.
background: West Ham were relegated last season under Nuno; Parker played 129 games for the club, captained it and has won three promotions as a manager with Fulham, Burnley and Bournemouth.

headline: Tony Mowbray steps back from Blackburn job for health reasons
facts: Blackburn announced on 17 November that Mowbray is stepping away.
Damien Johnson and Mike Dodds will handle first-team matters for now.
Blackburn are 13th in the Championship after a 2-1 win over West Ham.
background: Mowbray was diagnosed with bowel cancer in 2024 and left Birmingham; after an all-clear he coached West Brom and returned to Blackburn in June for a second spell.

headline: Sporting sack Rui Borges and move for Paulo Fonseca
facts: Sporting began talks to end Borges's contract and put Tiago Fernandes in temporary charge.
They agreed about 5 million euros in compensation with Lyon for Fonseca, 53.
Sporting are third, nine points behind Porto, and lost at home to LASK in the Champions League.
background: Borges took over in December 2024 after Amorim left and led Sporting to a title defence; last season Sporting lost to Arsenal in the Champions League quarterfinals.

headline: Sporting Kansas City fire Raphael Wicky after one season
facts: Wicky was fired after a last-place finish in the West with 26 points, the second-fewest in club history.
His record was 7-23-5 across all competitions.
The club will have its fourth coach since March 2025 when the sprint season starts in February.
background: Wicky is Swiss and previously coached Young Boys and Chicago Fire; Peter Vermes left early in 2025.

headline: What if Manchester United had hired Klopp instead of Moyes?
facts: The ESPN analysis says even a huge Klopp effect would not have given United a title since Ferguson.
With 10 extra points a season, United would have averaged 76 instead of 66 points and 3.8 instead of 5.3 finishing place.
Whoever replaces Carrick would be the ninth coach since Ferguson.
background: United are 14 seasons without a league title; Moyes, Van Gaal, Mourinho, Solskjaer, Ten Hag, Amorim and Carrick have followed Ferguson.

headline: Kovac says Dortmund must stop Kane together before Bayern clash
facts: Kovac called Kane sensational and said he cannot be stopped one on one.
Dortmund and Bayern were level on points at the top of the Bundesliga.
Dortmund had not beaten Bayern in their last five meetings, and Kompany was absent after his hospital stay.
background: Kane, the Ballon d'Or winner, was to be honoured by Bayern before the match.
footage_terms: Harry Kane Ballon d'Or Bayern honour

headline: Wrexham boss Phil Parkinson eases pressure with 4-1 win over Preston
facts: Wrexham beat bottom club Preston 4-1 with goals from Devine, Whiteman, Smith and Moore.
A 2-1 home loss to West Brom earlier had left them near the bottom, and Steven Gerrard had been linked with the job.
The win moved Wrexham up to 14th.
background: Whiteman, who scored against his former club Preston, was one of four scorers.

headline: Celtic's Martin O'Neill loses midfielder Mika Baur to a long injury
facts: O'Neill said Baur's injury is a blow because he was on fire.
Baur hurt his ankle in the win over Kilmarnock and faces a long spell out.
No return date was given.
background: O'Neill, 74, was made permanent Celtic manager in June 2026 on a one-year deal after the club sacked Wilfried Nancy 33 days into his job, and he managed Celtic from 2000 to 2005.

headline: Arteta faces a Saliba or Konsa selection dilemma at Arsenal
facts: Konsa has played well while Saliba was injured, so Arteta must choose or play them together.
Without Saliba, Arsenal's defensive line has sat at least a metre lower.
Konsa and Gabriel have made seven last-man tackles together this season, against five by Saliba and Gabriel in all of last season.
background: Konsa joined Arsenal from Aston Villa this summer for 55m pounds.

headline: Matthias Jaissle under pressure as Newcastle draw 1-1 at Fulham
facts: Murphy put Newcastle ahead on 80 minutes and Muniz equalised for Fulham on 83.
Newcastle have 12 points from 10 games and sit 12th.
Fulham, under Alvaro Arbeloa, were the better side for much of the match.
background: Newcastle's attack looked blunted in the draw, and a loss would have been their fifth of the season.

headline: Moyes keeps Everton's cup run going and backs Grealish discipline decision
facts: Everton beat Newcastle 3-1 in the Carabao Cup with goals from Garner, Hackney and Barry.
Grealish missed the game over a club discipline breach and Moyes said he supports the decision.
Everton now face League Two Fleetwood in the quarterfinal; they have not won a trophy since the 1995 FA Cup.
background: Arsenal, Chelsea, Manchester United and Aston Villa were already out of the competition.

headline: Hearts boss Vrancken gambles on a makeshift left-back to stop Mohamed Salah
facts: Hearts lost 2-0 away to Trabzonspor in the Conference League; Salah scored a penalty and set up the second goal.
Vrancken used Rogers Mato at left-back to mark Salah and admitted critics would blame him if Salah scored three.
Hearts came off a 7-1 defeat at Celtic and had one point from two Conference League games.
background: Vrancken was appointed Hearts head coach after Derek McInnes left for Rangers, and his European start included a 4-0 defeat to Graz in qualifying.
